title: Expository writing: reporting facts clearly
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Expository writing explains or informs. A report tells the reader true facts about a topic, in a clear order, without the writer's opinions getting in the way.
A fact can be checked and is true for everyone. An opinion is what one person feels or prefers.

steps: 'The sun is a star.' — this can be checked, so it is a fact.
'The sun is beautiful.' — this is a feeling, so it is an opinion.
A report is built from facts.

blocks.question: Which of these is a FACT?
blocks.explain: 'Trinidad is an island' can be checked and is true for everyone, so it is a fact.
blocks.rule: A fact can be checked and is true for everyone; an opinion is what someone feels.

practiceItems.prompt: fact or opinion: 'Blue is the best colour'
fact or opinion: 'Trinidad is an island'

blocks.content: Organise a report in order: open by naming the topic, give grouped facts in the middle, and close with a short summary.

blocks.instruction: Put the parts of a report in the correct order.
blocks.rule: A report opens with the topic, gives grouped facts in the middle, and closes with a summary.

practiceItems.prompt: the part of a report that names the topic (opening/middle/closing)
the part that gives the facts
the part that sums up at the end
what expository writing gives instead of opinions

blocks.question: Which sentence belongs in a factual report: 'Dogs have four legs' or 'Dogs are the best pets'?
options: 'Dogs have four legs' — it is a fact that can be checked
'Dogs are the best pets' — it sounds convincing
blocks.explain: A report gives facts — things that can be checked and are true for everyone. 'Dogs have four legs' can be checked. 'Dogs are the best pets' is an opinion; someone else might prefer cats. Reports stick to facts.
blocks.rule: A report uses facts (checkable), not opinions (personal views).
blocks.principle: Expository writing informs with facts, not the writer's feelings.
canonical_solution: A fact can be checked and is true for all
'Dogs have four legs' can be checked
So the fact belongs in the report

rubric.look_for: tests whether each statement can be checked
explains reports use facts, not opinions

misconceptions.coach: Sounding convincing does not make it a fact — can it be checked?
'best pets' is a view, so it is an opinion.

practiceItems.prompt: a statement that can be checked is a
'dogs have four legs' — fact or opinion?
'ice cream is the best' — fact or opinion?

blocks.content: Report the facts, keep opinions out, and organise from topic to summary. That is clear expository writing. Let's practise!
